chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father and Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari from Mansur ibn Hazim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Muqarrin (one who combines Hajj and Tamattu') is not considered a Muqarrin unless he brings the offering (Hady), and upon him are two circumambulations (Tawaf) of the House and a Sa'i between As-Safa and Al-Marwah, just as the Mufrid does, and there is no superiority for the Muqarrin over the Mufrid except by virtue of the offering.

key_terms.السَّعْيُ: The Sa'i (walking between Safa and Marwah)
key_terms.الْقَارِنُ: The Muqarrin, one who combines Hajj al-Qiran
key_terms.الْمُفْرِدُ: The Mufrid, one who performs Hajj al-Mufrid

ai.seo_question: What are the ritual requirements and status of the Muqarrin in Hajj according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq clarifies the ritual structure of Hajj al-Qiran, emphasizing that the pilgrim must perform two Tawafs and one Sa'i, mirroring the Mufrid but distinguished by the obligatory Hady. This ruling highlights the jurisprudential balance in Shia fiqh where the Qarin’s status is equal to the Mufrid, with the sole differentiator being the sacrificial offering, reflecting the practical application of combining Umrah and Hajj under a single Ihram.
